findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and has confusing, dead logic
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false when `enabled` is true, and returns false otherwise. Every path returns false, so the feature flag has no effect. This is probably the intent for a security stopgap, but the code is misleading: the inverted `enabled` variable and the redundant branch suggest the flag is honored when it is not. A future maintainer may 'fix' it and silently re-enable the vulnerable path. It should be a plain `return false` (or removed) with a comment explaining why SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: Execute and the SQL command are still reachable via the legacy node-building path
findings.body: The disable check lives only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (used by the older rawNode path) still calls `NewSQLCommand`, which calls `sql.TablesList`; that now fails with 'not implemented' and surfaces as the generic 'error reading SQL command'. This does not cause a vulnerability, but the two paths return different, misleading errors for the same disabled feature. A user hitting the legacy path is told their SQL is invalid rather than that SQL expressions are disabled. The disable check should be applied at one common place.

findings.title: No tests added for the disabled SQL expression behavior
findings.body: The PR changes SQL expression behavior (always rejected in the reader, stub DB returns 'not implemented'), but adds or updates no tests. Existing tests that rely on SQL expressions working, such as sql_command_test or parser tests that call `TablesList`, will now fail or need updating. Nothing asserts the new error from `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL`, so a regression that re-enables the path would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Stale DuckDB naming and misleading error text
findings.body: `TablesList` still uses a variable named `duckDB`, builds a DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command, and logs the raw SQL on error, even though the DuckDB dependency is gone. The stub's `RunCommands` always returns 'not implemented', so every call fails with 'error serializing sql: not implemented'. That message is confusing for operators. The leftover code is dead and misleading and should be removed or the function should return a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' error.
